outputs.explanation: Panel A is a schematic (breast anatomy drawing) plus a classification table; no averaged data plot is shown.
Panel B is a schematic diagram illustrating the study aim, with icons and text; no plot of data.
Panel C is a schematic illustrating the experimental setup (clock gene reporter, luciferase recording); no data plot present.

Panel D shows idealized/illustrative example traces (Model #1-3) inside a conceptual workflow diagram explaining the analysis approach, not measured data with averages — treated as schematic per the 'idealized curve in a model diagram' rule.
Panel E shows a generic illustrative correlation heatmap (placeholder labels 1-7) used to explain the analysis concept rather than present actual averaged data; treated as schematic.

Panel F shows illustrative example growth curves (Model 1-3) used to explain the concept of exponential growth rate quantification, not real averaged data with replicates; treated as schematic. Even if considered a line plot, line plots are exempt from this check.

Panel G shows illustrative example dose-response curves (Model 1-3) explaining the concept of growth inhibition metrics, not real averaged data; treated as schematic. Line plots are also exempt from this check.

Panel H shows illustrative example heatmap and mutation grid used to explain the genomic analysis workflow with generic placeholder axes, not real averaged data; treated as schematic. Heatmaps are also exempt from this check.

Panel I contains scatter plots (PCA cluster plot and 3D circadian phenotype plot) where each dot already represents an individual sample; scatter plots are exempt from requiring additional overlaid individual points.
